name: WaterPourVisual
src_typeComment: Two independent, combinable ways to SHOW a water pour — particles alone are cheap and read clearly as droplets; the shader stream alone is smoother and stays perfectly continuous even at very low pour rates where sparse particles would look broken up; both together give the densest look. This component only ever DRAWS whatever pour state it's handed via SetPour — it has no tilt/input logic of its own, so it stays reusable by anything that can compute a pour rate and an arc (typically WateringCanController).

src_serialized.name: waterColor
src_serialized.tooltip: Tint applied to both the particles and the stream.

src_serialized.name: maxEmissionRate
src_serialized.tooltip: Particles emitted per second at full pour rate (rate 1).

src_serialized.name: scrollSpeed
src_serialized.tooltip: How fast the flow texture scrolls along the stream — higher reads as faster-moving water.

src_members.sig: public void SetPour(bool isPouring, float rate01, Vector3[] arcPoints)
src_members.name: SetPour
src_members.comment: Called every frame by whatever is driving the pour — typically WateringCanController — so this component never has to know about tilt or input itself.
